script: Hey everyone, welcome to "Chillwave B2".
I'm Ethan.
Tonight, let’s chat about keeping in touch with family from afar.
My cousin video-called me last night from another country—same time we were both making dinner.
Heh, let’s keep it cozy and share some ideas on staying close, no matter the distance.
My aunt's in Texas, so we've been doing weekly Zoom calls since the pandemic hit.
We used to just sit and chat, but tech issues made it hard to keep the conversation going.
Last month, she suggested we play a board game online together—something called Catan.
We set up two laptops, passed our phones for camera control, and rolled dice like it was the same room.
The biggest win wasn't beating her, but laughing when the Wi-Fi cut out mid-turn. Heh.
How do you stay close with family when distance makes it tough?
My uncle started a group chat with the whole family—just for sharing random songs or funny clips.
He says it’s like having a little piece of everyone’s day, even if we’re spread out.
Last week, my cousin sent a clip of her cat knocking over a mug—total chaos, but it made us all laugh.
Sometimes we’ll all listen to the same song at the same time, just to feel connected.
Heh, I once ended a shift at work to a group dance party over text—totally awkward, but kinda perfect.
What’s a small but meaningful way you’ve kept in touch lately?
It’s amazing how these little rituals turn into traditions, right?
Even something like trading song links feels like sharing a piece of your day.
Heh, I bet some of you have your own weird but wonderful routines.
Maybe you’re video-calling while folding laundry or sending voice notes during your commute.
What’s a habit you’ve picked up that feels like family glue?
Let me know—next week, we’ll dive into more ways to keep the vibes warm.
Hey, you know, when you’re on a video call and someone says, “Let’s do this again soon,” you can respond with, “Count me in!”
It’s a casual way to say, “I’m definitely going to be there.”
My aunt said that to me after our Catan game, and I just replied, “Count me in!” because I knew I’d join the next one.
Another thing I’ve heard is, “We’ll catch up soon,” which is just a friendly way to promise a future chat.
Try these out next time you want to keep things positive and easy—sounds good, right? Heh.
"End of the night, but the texts and calls keep going—as long as we make time, the distance doesn’t matter. Heh."
"Thanks for tuning in, you know who you are—keeping it real together every week."
"Sleep tight, stay connected, and we’ll vibe again next week on Chillwave B2."
"Night-night, folks."
